comments.note: AC-1 FAIL: No test builds a persona with target='deep-agents'. The registry tests in target-registry.test.ts verify that defaultRegistry has the deep-agents entry with correct outputDirKey/filenameContextKey/contextFlags, but they never call build(), buildSuite(), or buildPersona() with 'deep-agents' as the active target. A build test must verify: (a) output file lands in outputDirs['deep-agents'], (b) output filename equals da_file_name, (c) DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER_DEEP_AGENTS is applied when no persona-level frontmatter is set, (d) target_deep_agents=true is injected into template context during the build.

AC-2 FAIL: No three-target integration test exists. build.test.ts covers vscode+claude-code at most. A three-target test must configure outputDirs for all three targets, pass targets: ['vscode', 'claude-code', 'deep-agents'], and assert that 3 results are returned with correct output paths for each. Without this test, the build() dispatcher for the deep-agents code path is entirely unexercised at the integration level.

Scope gap: target_deep_agents flag injection is not tested. target-variable-injection.test.ts covers target_vscode and target_claude_code injection, but has no tests for target_deep_agents. The WP-009 scope explicitly listed 'Test target_deep_agents flag injection'. This should be added alongside AC-1.

comments.note: [documentation-forward] tests/integration/build.test.ts file header (lines 1-15) only references WP-007 ACs. Two new describe blocks were added for WP-009 AC-1 and AC-2. Update the file header to note WP-009 additions so future contributors know the file covers both WPs.

[documentation-forward] The three-target integration test uses SAMPLE_SUITE_DIR (example-persona.yaml) which has no da_file_name field. The deep-agents output filename therefore falls back to 'example-persona.md' (contentBasename), sharing its basename with the Claude Code output. The test does not assert path.basename(daResult!.outputPath) — understandably, since AC-2 scope is routing correctness, not filename resolution. Add a brief comment ('// fixture has no da_file_name; output filename falls back to contentBasename') so the omission is clearly intentional.

createDeepAgentsSuite() in target-variable-injection.test.ts duplicates the directory scaffolding logic from createSuite() (mkdir meta, mkdir content, write _shared.yaml, write agent.yaml, write content.md). The two helpers differ only in their outputDirs vs outVscode/outClaudeCode configuration. Not blocking — the helpers serve different fixture configurations — but a shared factory accepting an outConfig option would reduce duplication if more target-specific suite helpers are added in future WPs.

No code is clean and consistent — the WP-009 additions integrate naturally with the existing test file structure. The deep-agents tests mirror the target_vscode/target_claude_code test patterns precisely, and the build.test.ts additions follow the same inner-describe + afterEach cleanup conventions as the pre-existing tests.
